title: Motion Observation Artifact (M2a)
description: What a page was seen to DO, and — separately — what caused it. Written by the motion-observation pass, which is independent of the forensic capture: it runs unfrozen, records timestamps, and is compared by classification rather than by bytes. Its contract version is separate so a change here can never invalidate a forensic capture.

$motionContract.description: Independent of CAPTURE_CONTRACT_VERSION. The two version different things.

apparatusRemaining.description: Elements still carrying an apparatus marker after cleanup. Asserted rather than assumed; anything but 0 means the page was left instrumented.

$motionStage.description: Versions the M2b stage sections below, independently of $motionContract. The sections are additive: a reader that knows only the M2a contract ignores them and loses nothing it previously had, which is why the contract version does not move.

openingSequence.description: The first meaningful visual sequence after load. Its `status` carries the distinction the whole artifact exists for: `none-detected` means the stage looked and saw nothing, `failed` means it could not finish looking, and `not-attempted` means it never ran. None of the three may be read as 'this page has no animation'.

reason.description: Required in substance whenever status is `failed` or `not-attempted`: a refusal without a stated reason is indistinguishable from a bug.

frames.description: One entry per sample. The cold-load recorder identifies a frame by its scheduled offset, which is exact and meaningful; the older three-frame path labelled them instead. Both shapes are accepted, and neither field is required, because a frame is identified by its position in this array either way.

atMs.description: When the sample was actually taken. It can lag the schedule on a busy main thread, which is why both are kept.

notDetected.description: Present only when status is `none-detected`. It records what WAS observable, so that 'nothing moved' can be told apart from 'we could not see movement of this kind'.

restoredFromCache.description: Null means unknown. Reporting false for an unmeasured cache state would assert a fresh load that was never confirmed.

coldLoad.description: What the cold load itself was, as opposed to what it saw. A reader who is told no animation was found needs these facts to judge whether that is a finding about the page or about the apparatus.

reducedMotion.description: `differs` is null unless a comparison actually ran. Reporting false for a comparison that never happened would assert that reduced motion changes nothing, which is a finding and not a default.

controls.description: Observations taken with no action, over comparable elapsed time. Without one, no causal claim can be licensed.

cleanup.description: What cleanup achieved, not what it attempted. Every key is present and starts null: a step that never ran and a step that ran and failed must be distinguishable.

reducedMotionRestored.description: Null when reduced motion was never changed. Reporting `true` for something untouched would claim a restoration that never happened.

elementState.description: One half of a change. Every property is optional because the sampler records what the page exposed; a property absent here was not read, which is not the same as a property that was read and found empty.

participant.description: One element seen to change during the opening sequence. `timingSource` is the field that keeps a screenshot from becoming a measurement: `sampled` means the timing came from timestamped frames, `declared` means it came from a stylesheet and states intent rather than outcome, and `none` means the change was seen and never timed.

timingSource.description: How the timing was obtained. `sampled-bounds` is the honest answer for frame sampling: the frames say the change had happened by one offset and had not by the previous one, which BOUNDS it without measuring it. `sampled` is reserved for a source that timed the change itself. Collapsing the two would turn a bound into a duration, which is the single easiest way for this artifact to lie.

firstChangeMs.description: The offset of the first sample that saw a difference.

lastChangeMs.description: The offset of the last sample that saw one.

approximateDurationMs.description: latestEnd minus earliestStart. An upper bound, never an exact duration.

participantTrigger.description: Deliberately NOT `triggerClassification`. That record answers 'did this action cause this change', for an action the apparatus performed. This one additionally names WHICH trigger, from a closed vocabulary, and applies to a participant whose action may be page load — something no apparatus performs. Reusing one shape for both would force a null action into a field that means 'the action we took'.

trigger.description: Null whenever the classification is `unverified`. A trigger name and an unverified classification together would let a reader take the name and drop the caveat.

reason.description: Required in substance whenever the classification is `unverified`.

claimType.description: `runtime-observation` says a state changed. It does NOT say why. A causal statement lives only in triggerClassification.

monotonicMs.description: From a monotonic clock, so elapsed time survives a wall-clock adjustment.

motionEvidenceClass.description: The motion-specific evidence axis, separate from the five-value STATUS vocabulary, which is unchanged.

controlObservationId.description: The control that licensed any causal claim on this record. Null means no causal claim can be made from it.

triggerClassification.description: Null on a control record — a control that classified its own trigger would be evidence for itself.
A causal claim, or an explicit refusal to make one. `verified` requires a control that saw no change over comparable elapsed time.

reason.description: Required in substance whenever the classification is `unverified`: a refusal with no stated reason is indistinguishable from an oversight.
